subject: Escrow request and partial payment flow for held invoices 4729/4730
messages:
From: Sara Hale <sara@apexlogix.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: ProcureCo AP <procureco@procureco.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Payment hold on invoices 4729 / 4730 — escrow requirement

Hi Vanessa,

Quick heads up — our procurement team has placed invoices 4729 and 4730 on hold while legal reviews a cross-border VAT clause. They are requesting that final settlement be routed to an escrow account (ProcureCo is handling the escrow).

We want to avoid a full subscription interruption. Two constraints from their side: (1) they want an escrow agreement signed before funds are released, and (2) they prefer to release payment in two tranches (60% / 40%) once escrow conditions are met. Also: the card on file for this account is a corporate card that rotates (their corporate T&E program renews cards monthly), so they asked whether Redwood can support a rapid token rotation so ProcureCo can initiate payment from the new token once escrow releases the first tranche.

Can Redwood confirm the following:
- Whether you can accept a split-settlement (two captures) against the two invoice IDs, or if we need to issue new invoice numbers for each tranche.
- A recommended flow for rotating the stored payment method token (the buyer prefers not to re-enter card details through our UI).
- If Redwood can be available to respond to any Stripe or acquirer inquiries — ProcureCo will share a brief decline log with you if their attempt fails.

I attached the two invoice PDFs and the procurement contact info. Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Thanks,
Sara Hale\VP, Finance\ApexLogix

[Attachment: invoice-4729.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: invoice-4730.pdf (PDF)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sara Hale <sara@apexlogix.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Payment hold on invoices 4729 / 4730 — escrow requirement

Sara —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. We'll support a two-tranche collection and coordinate the token rotation with Stripe if the buyer prefers not to re-enter card details. High-level plan:

1) Split capture approach: we can either (A) perform two separate captures against the existing invoices (capture1 = 60% of combined balance, capture2 = remaining 40%) or (B) issue two new invoice numbers and capture each separately. Option A is preferable from your side if you want to keep the same invoice references; Option B is cleaner for reconciliation if ProcureCo requires discrete payment references. Please confirm ProcureCo's preference.

2) Token rotation: Ben (payments) will propose the safest flow. Typical approach is a short-lived SetupIntent (or SetupAttempt) initiated by Redwood to attach the new PaymentMethod token that ProcureCo's PSP provides, then swap the default PaymentMethod on the customer object and trigger the capture. If the PSP cannot provide a token, we can accept a one-time card-on-file provided through a secure link.

3) Chargeback/decline handling: if ProcureCo's first attempt hits a decline or an acquirer inquiry, we will document the evidence immediately and open a prioritized support request with Stripe Escalations. Please forward the decline log as soon as you have it.

Ben / Markus — can you confirm the exact Stripe API steps we should ask ProcureCo to follow and whether we need new invoice IDs to meet accounting requirements? Also flag any KYC or PCI uplift required for this flow.

Vanessa
VP, Customer Success Operations\Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Hale <sara@apexlogix.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Payment hold on invoices 4729 / 4730 — escrow requirement

Following up with the technical plan — copying Sara so ProcureCo and ApexLogix can see the steps.

What we can do from Redwood's side:
- Option A (preferred if reconciliation is okay): capture twice against invoice 4729/4730 using two separate capture calls (we'll record metadata capture.part=1 and capture.part=2). That keeps invoice numbers unchanged.
- Option B: generate invoice-4729-T1 and invoice-4729-T2 (or equivalent) if ProcureCo insists on separate invoice refs. Both are supported.

Token rotation / capture flow we recommend (Stripe-native):
1) ProcureCo's PSP creates a PaymentMethod token for the new card and sends the token to Redwood via the secure channel (we can accept it via an encrypted SFTP drop or via a Stripe SetupIntent response webhook).
2) Redwood creates a SetupIntent referencing the existing customer and attaches the incoming PaymentMethod token (if needed).
3) Once attached, we call PaymentIntent.capture for the agreed amount (60% first).
4) On second tranche, repeat capture for remaining 40%.

If ProcureCo cannot provide a token, we will generate a short-lived hosted payment session (PCI-compliant) to capture the new card.

If a decline occurs during tranche 1:
- Please immediately send the decline details to escalations@stripe.com and copy us. Include the decline_code, acquirer_response_code, and the attempted PaymentIntent ID.
- We'll assemble evidence (contract, signed escrow agreement, invoices) in a chargeback-defensive bundle.

Attached: minimal decline log sample format we need from ProcureCo (stripe-decline-log.csv).

Ben
Payments Ops\Redwood Inference
[Attachment: stripe-decline-log.csv (CSV)]
